title: What the Singularity Index is
description: The index does not hold the world's information; it holds a map of where the world's information is indexed. A question arrives once, the singularity layer consults its map of indexes, translates the question for each relevant index, gathers answers, and merges them into one ranked result. The underlying indexes stay independent and keep their own data.

architecture: A coverage-map store describing participating indexes; a query planner that selects indexes per question; per-index translators; a result merger with provenance.

title: Index selection algorithm
description: Given a question, the planner picks which indexes to ask. It scores each index on topical overlap, expected freshness, query-language fit, and historical answer quality for similar questions. Asking every index every time is wasteful; asking too few misses answers. The selection balances coverage against cost.

demo.title: Runnable code demo — Index selection algorithm

architecture: Feature-based scorer per (question, index); cost model per index query; top-k selection with diversity bonus so similar indexes do not crowd out different ones.

title: Merged result ranking and retrieval
description: Answers from different indexes arrive with incompatible scores. The merger normalizes scores per index, deduplicates near-identical answers found in several indexes, and re-ranks by a unified relevance model trained on cross-index judgments. Duplicates collapse into one answer with multiple provenance trails.

title: Failure modes: index outages and map rot
description: Indexes go down, change their APIs, or quietly rot their coverage. The layer detects outages via the prober, marks stale coverage maps, routes around dead indexes, and tells the caller what was skipped. A merged answer list that silently dropped an index is a lie; the layer reports the gap.

title: Scaling: hierarchical singularity layers
description: One layer cannot map every index on Earth. Regional singularity layers map local indexes and federate upward: a continental layer queries regional layers the way regional layers query indexes. Coverage maps compose — a region's map is the union of its indexes' maps — so planning works at every level.

title: Security: querying across trust boundaries
description: Indexes have different access rules; a unified query must not leak restricted answers to unauthorized callers. The layer evaluates each caller's permissions per index, filters at the source where possible, and redacts at merge when necessary. Every merged answer carries the permission context it was computed under.

demo.title: Runnable code demo — Security: querying across trust boundaries

architecture: Per-index permission evaluation; source-side filtering preferred; merge-time redaction; permission context attached to cached merged results.
